tutorials.title: Set up Alipay before you fly
tutorials.why: Most shops, taxis and metro gates in China take mobile payment only. Setting up at home on Wi-Fi takes 10 minutes and avoids doing it jet-lagged with no data.
steps: Install Alipay from the App Store or Google Play. Outside China it opens in English automatically.
Sign up with your own mobile number (any country) and enter the SMS code. No Chinese number or Chinese bank account is needed.
Tap Me > Bank Cards > Add Now. Set a 6-digit payment password, then add one mainstream credit card: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Discover, Diners Club or UnionPay.
Tap Me > Settings > Account & Security > Identity Verification. Upload your passport photo page and do the face check. Do this now, not later.
tutorials.fallback: If the card will not link, see Card won't link. If you prefer not to link a card, open TourCard inside Alipay as a prepaid wallet.

tutorials.title: eSIM installed but no internet after landing
tutorials.why: Nine times out of ten the eSIM is fine and one switch is off: Data Roaming. Travel eSIMs count as roaming, so the phone refuses to use them until you allow it.
steps: Open Settings > Cellular (Mobile Data) on iPhone, or Settings > Network & internet > SIMs on Android. Set Cellular Data to the eSIM line, then turn Data Roaming ON for that line.
Turn Airplane Mode on for a few seconds and off again so the phone re-registers with the local tower.
If it still says No Service, open the eSIM line's settings and enter the APN from the confirmation email, then restart the phone.
Check the plan is activated: some eSIMs activate on first connection, others at a start date you chose.
tutorials.fallback: Connect to the airport Wi-Fi to reach the eSIM seller's 24/7 chat (Trip.com has one), or buy a physical SIM at the arrivals counter with your passport.

tutorials.title: Airport Wi-Fi asks for a phone number
tutorials.why: Public Wi-Fi in China requires identity verification by law. Airports accept an SMS code to many foreign numbers; shops and malls usually accept only Chinese numbers.
steps: Join the airport network: Pudong #AIRPORTPVG-FREE-WIFI, Beijing Capital AIRPORT-FREE-WIFI-NEW, Daxing BDIA-FREE-WIFI. The login page opens by itself; if not, open any website.
Choose the overseas or international phone option, pick your country code, type your number and tap Get code (获得验证码). The SMS arrives on your roaming line even with data off.
Enter the code and tap Login (登录). The session lasts a few hours; reconnect the same way if it drops.
No code after a minute: do not keep tapping. All three airports' login pages have a Passport Login option where you photograph your passport instead; Beijing Capital also has passport kiosks.
tutorials.fallback: Airport information desks and the Payment Service Center in the arrivals hall help in person; ask for 免费WiFi.

tutorials.title: Get airport Wi-Fi with your passport
tutorials.why: Every major airport has a way to log in without any phone number. The login page at Pudong, Beijing Capital and Daxing has a Passport Login option where you photograph your passport; Beijing Capital additionally has kiosks that scan the passport and print a username and password.
steps: On the Wi-Fi login page tap Passport Login (护照登录), photograph the passport photo page in good light with all four corners visible, then take the selfie if asked and confirm.
Beijing Capital alternative: find the Wi-Fi kiosk (无线上网身份验证自助终端). Show staff this line if needed: 请问最近的无线上网身份验证自助终端在哪里?
Open the passport to the photo page and slide it into the slot marked 护照扫码口 Passport Scanning. A slip prints with a username and password.
Type them into 输入账号 (username) and 输入密码 (password) on the login page, then tap 登录.
tutorials.fallback: Beijing Capital slips last 5 hours, max 3 per passport. At Pudong the kiosks are all past security in departures, so arriving passengers should use the passport-photo login or ask the information desk; Wi-Fi service line (+86) 400 920 1851.

tutorials.title: Set up DiDi before you fly
tutorials.why: DiDi is China's Uber. Since 2026 the mainland app registers with a foreign number and takes international cards, but solving an SMS or card problem is far easier at home than outside an airport with luggage.
steps: Install DiDi China (the mainland app, not DiDi Rider which serves other countries). Pick English in the first screen.
Tap Account and sign in with your own mobile number; select your country code, not +86. Enter the SMS code.
Tap Account > Wallet > Payment Methods and add a Visa or Mastercard credit card, or choose Alipay if you already linked a card there.
If the app asks for identity verification, complete it with your passport now rather than at the airport.
tutorials.fallback: If DiDi will not register, skip the app: in Alipay search DiDi or tap Transport > Taxi; it uses your Alipay account and needs no Chinese number.

tutorials.title: Where to meet a DiDi at the airport
tutorials.why: Ride-hailing cars cannot stop at the arrivals kerb. Every major airport has a signed pickup zone, usually a numbered bay in a car park, and the app will not match you until you are near it.
steps: Collect your luggage first; do not book from the plane or the baggage hall.

Follow the signs reading Online Car-hailing / 网约车 to the pickup zone. At Pudong T2 the signs say 网约车上车点请前往P2停车库: take the lift down into the P2 car park and follow the 网约车 signs to a numbered waiting point (等候点). Ignore anyone offering a ride inside the terminal.
Open DiDi at the zone. It auto-selects the airport pickup spot; if the pin is across the road, drag it to your bay and note the bay code (such as A1 or B3).
Type the hotel name in English, pick Express or, with big luggage, the Airport Transfer car type, then confirm. Follow the in-app arrow to your bay.
tutorials.fallback: If no cars are matching, walk to the official taxi queue: at Pudong T2 follow the 出租车 Taxi signs down to level 1. A pre-booked Trip.com transfer avoids all of this: the driver waits at arrivals with your name.

tutorials.title: Set up WeChat Pay before you fly
tutorials.why: Some small shops and street stalls only take WeChat Pay. Setting it up at home avoids the friend-verification step, which is hard to complete once you are travelling alone.
steps: Install WeChat and sign up with your own mobile number (any country). Enter the SMS code.
When WeChat asks for security verification, choose the option to add a payment card and activate Weixin Pay; it is easier than finding an existing user to scan your QR code.
Go to Me > Services > Wallet > Cards > Add a Card and add a Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Discover or Diners Club card issued outside mainland China. A small verification charge is taken.
Set the 6-digit payment password when prompted and keep it; every payment asks for it.
tutorials.fallback: If the card step fails, finish Alipay first and come back to WeChat later; most travellers manage with Alipay alone.

tutorials.title: WeChat asks for your passport (Verify ID Info)
tutorials.why: Payments above a small total need real-name verification. The form asks for ID type, passport number, dates, nationality, address and occupation.
steps: On Verify ID Info choose ID type Passport and enter the number, country and expiry exactly as printed.
Fill the remaining fields: address can be your hotel, occupation any honest option. Empty fields block the Next button.
Upload the passport photo page in good light and complete the face scan facing a window.
If the screen says Risk exists in this operation, stop, wait, and see Risk control.
tutorials.fallback: Verification can take up to a day. Pay with Alipay or cash meanwhile; contact WeChat Pay support from Me > Services > Wallet > Customer Service Center if it stays pending.
